feature_request: create a d.py that prints hello ibm bob
acceptance_criteria: The system must create a new file named d.py in the designated directory.
The d.py script must be a valid Python module that can be executed without syntax errors.
Executing d.py must print the exact string 'hello ibm bob' to standard output.
plan: d.py already exists on disk, so we must MODIFY it (not create it). Specify and implement the change behavior as a pure side-effect when module is imported/executed: prepare a small, self-contained print statement (no side effects beyond the desired output) that writes exactly 'hello ibm bob' to standard output via print() and call it immediately in module scope (so that both 'python d.py' and 'import d' produce the expected stdout). Use plain string literal (no uppercasing, no case alterations).
